relationships.related_name: Yachtzentrum Greifswald GmbH (former East German boat/repair yard)
relationships.evidence_note: Michael Schmidt took over a former East German boat and repair yard operating as Yachtzentrum Greifswald before launching series yacht production in 1993.
Founder Michael Schmidt sold his stake to Aurelius SE (Munich investment holding) in 2011 and departed the company.
HanseYachts AG acquired Dehler Yachtbau (including Dehler and Varianta brands) out of insolvency in May 2009.
HanseYachts acquired the English Moody sailing yacht brand in 2007.
HanseYachts acquired Norwegian powerboat maker Fjord Boats AS in 2006.

series_production_evidence: Series production of the Hanse 291 launched at the 1993 Hamburg Boat Show; HanseYachts AG is a publicly listed (Frankfurt General Standard, since 2007) large-volume series sailing/motor yacht manufacturer currently producing sailboats under the Hanse and Dehler brands from Greifswald.

relationships.evidence_note: Dutch Neptunus Group took control 1998-2004 after Dehler's first bankruptcy filing.
Sold to Dutch businessman Wilan van den Berg in 2004.
German private equity firm acquired a minority stake in 2007; Dehler subsequently purchased Belgium-based ETAP Yachting before a second bankruptcy in 2008-2009.
HanseYachts AG acquired the Dehler brand out of creditors/insolvency in May 2009; production relocated from Freienohl to Greifswald in 2012.

series_production_evidence: Founded 1963 by Willi and Heinz Dehler producing dinghies, then the Varianta sailboat from 1966 in Freienohl; continuous series sailboat production (now 6 models, 29-46 ft) as a HanseYachts AG subsidiary using GRP construction since the 1960s.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Wikipedia/official history states current lineup is six sailing yacht models, 29-46 feet.

ambiguity_notes: Dehler is a brand/production line now operated as part of HanseYachts AG rather than an independently operating legal entity; retained as its own record because it has a distinct multi-decade production and ownership history prior to acquisition.

relationships.evidence_note: Bain Capital acquired Bavaria for an estimated 1.1-1.3 billion Euros in 2007.
Following the 2008 crash, Anchorage Advisors and Oaktree Capital Management each took a 45% stake in October 2009.
After an April 2018 bankruptcy filing, CMP acquired Bavaria as new investor in September 2018.
Bavaria acquired French catamaran producer Nautitech in 2014.

series_production_evidence: Founded 1978 by Winfried Herrmann and Josef Meltl in Giebelstadt; grew to producing ~3,500 sailing/motor yachts by 2006 with 600 employees, described as the largest yacht yard in Germany; continuous series GRP sailboat production to present.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Historical cumulative production ~3,500 boats by 2006; current active sailboat model count (30-56ft range per one source) not independently itemized from fetched pages.

ambiguity_notes: A separate production/assembly presence in Croatia (sometimes referred to loosely online as 'Bavaria Composites Croatia') was investigated but no independent evidentiary source confirming a distinct legal entity or factory was found; not included as a separate record to avoid inventing an entity.

relationships.evidence_note: Elan operates as a group; sailing yachts and skis are made in Slovenia, snowboards in Austria, motor yachts in Croatia, per Wikipedia.

relationships.related_name: Merrill Lynch International / Wiltan Enterprises Limited
relationships.evidence_note: In 2015 Slovenia's state holding (SDH) approved sale of state-owned Elan to Merrill Lynch International and Wiltan Enterprises Limited.

series_production_evidence: Founded 1945 (boatbuilding from 1949) by Rudi Finžgar in Begunje na Gorenjskem; adopted GRP/polyester in 1962, carbon-epoxy composites from 1978, VAIL vacuum infusion process from 2003; continuous series sailboat production (peak >300 boats/year in 2006-2007) to present under Elan d.o.o.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Current model count not itemized in fetched pages; historical peak production >300 boats/year (2006-2007).

ambiguity_notes: Elan is a multi-division group (skis in Slovenia, snowboards in Austria, motor yachts in Croatia, sailing yachts in Slovenia). This record covers only the sailing-yacht-producing entity/division 'Elan Yachts' under Elan d.o.o., Begunje na Gorenjskem, Slovenia.

aliases: Beneteau First (post-acquisition rebrand of Seascape model line)

relationships.evidence_note: Groupe Beneteau acquired 60% majority stake on July 9, 2018; founders Andraž Mihelin and Kristian Hajnšek retained 40%.

Seascape model designs (14, 18, 24, 27) formed the basis of the renewed Beneteau First performance-cruiser line; specialist press refers to resulting boats as 'Seascape/First' dual-named during the transition, e.g. 'Beneteau First 27 a.k.a Seascape 27'.

series_production_evidence: Founded 2008 by Mini Transat sailors Andraž Mihelin and Kristian Hajnšek in Slovenia; series-built transportable performance cruisers, e.g. Seascape 18 named 2010 European Yacht of the Year; majority-acquired by Beneteau in 2018 with production folded into the Beneteau First line.

sources.title: Think Seascape: Sailing the new Beneteau First 27
Beneteau takes over Seascape: First milestone for the renewal of the First series

rights_assessment.robots_or_api_notes: Press release page, likely intended for redistribution/citation

model_yield_estimate.notes: Seascape 14, 18, 24, and 27 were the pre-acquisition series models per Beneteau/YACHT coverage.

ambiguity_notes: Exact current legal/brand status is genuinely ambiguous in available sources: coverage through 2018-2019 shows dual naming ('Seascape/First') during transition, and no fetched source definitively states whether 'Seascape' still exists as an active standalone brand name today or has been fully folded into 'Beneteau First'. Recorded as acquired/production_transferred_to rather than asserting full merger, per instruction not to silently collapse two brand identities.

relationships.evidence_note: AD Boats was founded in 2002 as an extension of AD Plastik Ltd (automotive components manufacturer); AD Boats has operated as an autonomous company since January 2003.
One secondary source states Salona was acquired by German-Slovenian company Prevent Grupe; not independently corroborated by an official source in this research pass.

relationships.related_name: Groupe Beneteau (via Ostroda Yachts sp. z o.o.)
relationships.evidence_note: Groupe Beneteau acquired an 80% stake in Delphia Yachts through Polish subsidiary Ostroda Yachts sp. z o.o., closing November 30, 2018 in a newly formed entity 'Stocznia Jachtowa Delphia sp. z o.o.'; founding Kot brothers retained 20% via Delphia Yachts Kot sp. j.

series_production_evidence: Founded 1990 by brothers Piotr and Wojciech Kot in Olecko, Poland; officially renamed Delphia Yachts in 2003; grew to Poland's largest sailboat manufacturer at >150 units/year before 80% acquisition by Groupe Beneteau in 2018, continuing to design/build/market sailing and motor yachts under Delphia Yachts and Maxi Yachts brands.

rights_assessment.robots_or_api_notes: Corporate press release, likely intended for citation

model_yield_estimate.notes: >150 units/year production rate reported pre-acquisition; exact current model line count not captured (boat-delphia.com history page could not be retrieved -- returned unrelated hijacked/parked-domain content during this research pass).

ambiguity_notes: The claim that Delphia began as 'Sportlake' making small sailing boats from 1990 appears in one secondary source (itboat.com) but could not be corroborated against an official Delphia source, since boat-delphia.com/history/ returned unrelated gambling-site content when fetched (likely a domain/hosting issue at fetch time, not necessarily reflective of the real current site). Listed as an alias with a caveat rather than asserted as fact.

relationships.related_name: Ostródzkie Zakłady Szkutniczo-Drzewne (Ostróda Wooden Shipbuilding Workshops)
relationships.evidence_note: Wooden boat production under this name began in 1952 from a repair/woodworking facility tied to the Elbląg Canal.
Became independent entity 'Ostróda Yacht' Sp. z o.o. in 1994 after cooperation with Jeanneau began in 1992; acquired by Groupe Beneteau in 2001.

series_production_evidence: Continuous boatbuilding lineage from a 1952 state wood/repair yard through independent incorporation in 1994 to a present-day Beneteau Group production facility building >30 models and ~4,000 units/year under Jeanneau, Beneteau, Lagoon, Prestige, Monte Carlo Yachts and O'Hara brands (including sailing yachts).

model_yield_estimate.notes: Official page states 'more than 30 models of motor and sailing yachts' at ~4,000 units/year total across all brands produced at the site; sailing-only subset not separately itemized.

ambiguity_notes: Ostróda Yacht is the Polish production/legal entity within Groupe Beneteau that also served as the acquiring vehicle for Delphia Yachts; its own output is now overwhelmingly Beneteau-group brands (Jeanneau/Beneteau/etc.) rather than an independent Ostróda-branded product line, so entity_kind includes 'yard' in spirit but the record is kept as a distinct manufacturer/legal_organization because of its 70+ year independent production lineage prior to full group integration.

series_production_evidence: Family-owned shipyard in Radom, Poland producing a series line of polyester-GRP sailboats (Antila 22, 24.4, 26.2, 28.2, 30.1, 33.3); models have won industry awards including 'Yacht of the Year 2018' (Antila 24.4) and European boat-show recognitions.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Official site lists 5 current sailboat models: Antila 24.4, 26.2, 28.2, 30.1, 33.3.

ambiguity_notes: The official site describes the company as built on '30 years of business experience in the private sector' but does not state the shipyard's own founding year; company registry search found a November 4, 2011 registration date in one secondary source, used here as an estimated start_year. No founder name is disclosed on the official site.

relationships.evidence_note: Founder Krzysztof Stepniak began with an Ajoi charter business and small equipment-repair garage in 2000, reinvesting profit into own manufacturing.

series_production_evidence: Northman shipyard founded 1995 in Węgorzewo, Poland; launched sailing-yacht brand Maxus in 2007 with the Maxus 33, designed by naval architect Jacek Daszkiewicz; currently produces ~150 sailing/motor yachts per year, with models winning European Yacht of the Year nominations (e.g., Maxus 26 in 2016).

model_yield_estimate.notes: ~150 sailing and motor yachts/year combined output across Maxus, Northman, and Nexus brand lines; sailing-only Maxus model count not itemized from fetched pages.

ambiguity_notes: Northman is the shipyard/legal manufacturer; Maxus is its sailing-yacht brand (Northman and Nexus are separate motor-yacht brand lines from the same yard). Recorded as one combined manufacturer/brand record per instructions' semantic rule since evidence shows Maxus has no separate legal identity from the Northman shipyard.

relationships.evidence_note: Balt-Yacht is a longstanding manufacturing partner for Brunswick Marine, producing Quicksilver and Uttern motorboats under contract alongside its own-brand cruising and sailing boats.

series_production_evidence: Founded 1990 by Krystyna and Benedykt Kozłowski in Augustów, Poland; series GRP boat manufacturer of cruising and semi-planing boats (7-12m), own sailing/cruising boat lines plus contract production; SunCamper 30 won Polish Yacht of the Year 2011 and Balt 818 Tytan won Polish Yacht of the Year 2015.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Official site fetch failed (TLS certificate error) during this research pass; model count taken only from search-result summaries, not independently itemized.

ambiguity_notes: Balt-Yacht produces both own-brand cruising/sailing boats and contract-manufactured motorboats (Quicksilver/Uttern) for Brunswick; the specific proportion of sailboat vs. powerboat models in current production was not confirmed because the official site (baltyacht.pl) could not be retrieved via WebFetch (certificate error). Retained on the strength of the specialist secondary source and prior 'Balt 818 Tytan'/'SunCamper 30' sailing/cruising boat award evidence.

relationships.evidence_note: Original carpentry business founded 1875 by Gottfried I. Schöchl; grandsons began building clinker boats in 1950 and obtained an official boat-building license in 1957 before series GRP/polyester production began in 1961.
Restructured under third-generation leader Andreas Schöchl in 2021 as 'Sunbeam Watersports GmbH'.

series_production_evidence: Series sailboat production began in 1961 (polyester/epoxy resin construction) in Mattsee-Unternberg, Austria; the 'Sunbeam' brand name established with the Sunbeam 22 in 1968 and continues on current models (Sunbeam 23, 24, Manta 19); won Yacht of the Year awards in 2017 and 2019; ~35 employees as of most recent data.

model_yield_estimate.notes: Current lineup per Wikipedia: Sunbeam 23, Sunbeam 24, Manta 19 (22-32.1 ft range); historical models up to 46 ft also existed.

ambiguity_notes: Legal entity name changed to 'Sunbeam Watersports GmbH' in 2021; official current-site URL could not be independently confirmed/fetched in this research pass (only the German Wikipedia article was retrieved), so official_current_site is left null rather than guessed.

series_production_evidence: GRP/laminate sailboat manufacturer headquartered in Veverská Bítýška near Brno, Czech Republic, producing an 'A' series model line (A45, A35, A34, A32, A29, A25, A23/Costa) supplied at various completion stages from bare hull to turnkey.

model_yield_estimate.notes: 7 named A-series models listed on official site: A45, A35, A34, A32, A29, A25, A23 (Costa).

ambiguity_notes: Direct conflict between sources on founding date: the official website's marketing copy states the brand/tradition dates to 1984, while a company-registry secondary source gives the legal entity's (s.r.o.) registration date as May 12, 2009 (IČO 28337221). Both figures are preserved here rather than silently resolved; production_era.start_year uses the earlier claimed date with basis 'estimated' and this conflict is flagged for human review. It is also unclear from available sources whether these are true fixed series models or semi-custom/build-to-order boats built on repeated hull molds; series_production_evidence reflects the latter possibility explicitly.
